Secondary diagnoses: Back pain / spine (chronic opioid; benzo); Non-obstructive CAD (<50%) / coronary calcium (88% stenosis; CAC score 514); Non-kidney organ transplant (20.4 yrs ago; organ liver); cataracts

Reason for Admission: Evaluation and management of frailty findings and follow-up for liver transplant.

Hospital Course:
Mr. Green, a 78-year-old male, was admitted for evaluation and management of frailty findings. The patient has a history of a liver transplant 20.4 years ago, currently controlled, and is on immunosuppressive therapy. He also presents with back pain managed with chronic opioids and benzodiazepines, non-obstructive coronary artery disease with 88% stenosis and a coronary calcium score of 514, and cataracts.

During his hospital stay, Mr. Green underwent a comprehensive evaluation, including a review of his current medications and assessment of his frailty status. His back pain was managed with his ongoing medication regimen, and no acute changes were noted in his coronary artery disease or liver transplant status. Ophthalmology consultation confirmed the presence of cataracts, with no acute changes or complications.

The hospital course was uneventful. Mr. Green remained stable throughout his stay, with no new symptoms or complications arising. He was and participated in physical therapy aimed maintaining his functional status. His vital signs remained within normal limits, with blood pressure recorded at 112/66 mmHg and weight at 191 pounds on admission.

Discharge Plan:
Mr. Green was home in stable condition. He was advised to continue with his current medication regimen, including tacrolimus 1 mg and mycophenolate 500 mg for immunosuppression post-liver transplant. He was instructed to follow up with his primary care physician for routine monitoring and management of his chronic conditions. Additionally, he was referred to an ophthalmologist for further evaluation and potential surgical intervention for his cataracts.

Social History:
Mr. Green has a history of current tobacco use, smoking approximately 2 cigarettes per day, a habit he started on 01/23/1974. He consumes about 10 alcoholic drinks per week. His family history is significant for type 2 diabetes in his father, who was diagnosed at age 62.

Follow-Up:
Mr. Green is scheduled for a follow-up appointment with Dr. Cole Hunter at

Collier Group Medical Group to monitor his frailty status, liver transplant function, and manage his back pain and coronary artery disease. He is also encouraged to maintain a healthy lifestyle, including smoking cessation and moderation of alcohol consumption.
